steps.instruction:
READ Jane Austen, Emma. Locator: Volume 1, chapters 1–3. https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/jane-austen/emma
Edition/use note: 1815 novel; Standard Ebooks edition, Gutenberg158 transcription. US public-domain/CC0 statement checked. Three volumes:18,18,19 chapters.

READ William Shakespeare, The Merchant of Venice. Locator: I.i–iii. https://shakespeare.mit.edu/merchant/full.html
Edition/use note: MIT Shakespeare electronic text of the public-domain play; external reading only. Use act/scene locators, not screen page numbers.

WORD STUDY, week1, within the existing reading/conference slot: Latin videre, to see: vision, visible. Greek logos, word/account/reason: logic, biology. Match each supplied form/meaning to its two derivatives; explain the relationship in your own words. These romanized forms support etymology; they do not substitute for a full Latin/Greek reading course or establish pronunciation proficiency. Check current meanings in context. A word's history is evidence about its history, not a rule that every derivative retains the exact ancient sense. Existing optional faith-language work remains separate.

Adult previews readings for antisemitism, coercion, enslavement, executions, crime, accounts of suicide and religious controversy. For North's final death accounts and Julius Caesar's violent scenes, preview the exact pages/scenes and omit graphic method details from oral reading or use a neutral account of the outcome. No reenactment or personal disclosure. Explain prejudice without reenacting it or asking a learner to defend a group identity. In Merchant, distinguish a character's slur from the tutor's speech; do not require a learner to speak slurs. Omit abusive words aloud, not the fact that the text contains prejudice. For distress, stop and use an adult's neutral synopsis for analysis, marking that as a supported route rather than independent reading of omitted text. Read Everyman's theology historically; faith, character and assent are never scored.

TEACH inference and its limits. Read in four short sessions away from the device where possible. After each section close the book and narrate events/argument in order; reopen to correct omissions. Keep three columns: exact textual observation, inference, question. Ask one Socratic question at a time; wait for a first response before another prompt. Context aids reading but must not replace it. Composition develops from a supported evidence paragraph into a sustained essay; do not require a full essay before its structure has been taught. Word ranges are flexible planning guides, not pass/fail thresholds. Adjust to actual entry evidence while preserving the objective. Edition reconciliation: Emma VolumeII chapter1 is continuous chapter19; VolumeIII chapter1 is continuous chapter37. Use the student's volume/chapter plus continuous number when needed. Yonge reader part is story chapter plus1. Shakespeare act/scene is stable; line numbers vary and are not required. North page numbers are the printed1909 numbers, not PDF screen indices. A different edition needs a logged chapter/speaker/paragraph match before assignment; never mark a correct equivalent locator wrong for pagination alone.
